modeButton__exploreCurrent__tooltip: Explore current world terrestrial ecosystems. Three smaller map views below show the landform, land cover, and climate contributing to each distinct ecosystem.
modeButton__projection__tooltip: Explore how ecosystems may change by 2050, based on the projections of two divergent global climate models.
projectionTypeButton__sustainableModel__: A scenario where the world shifts toward environmentally friendly practices, develops toward lower inequality. Assumes a rapid decline in greenhouse gas emissions.
projectionTypeButton__regionalRivalsMode: A scenario defined by slow economic growth and material-intensive consumption that will likely double the amount of current CO2 by 2100.
projectionFilterButton__aridity__tooltip: Areas projected to increase in aridity by 2050
projectionFilterButton__temperature__too: Areas projected to increase in temperature  by 2050
projectionFilterButton__landCover__toolt: Areas where land cover type is expected to change by 2050
projectionFilterButton__anyChange__toolt: Areas where aridity, temperature, or land cover are expected to change by 2050
projectionFilterButton__allChanges__tool: Areas where aridity, temperature, and land cover are all expected to change by 2050
landformMiniMap__tooltip: In the context of ecosystem settings, landforms are areas of similar topographic character based on elevation range, slope, and the distribution of upland and lowland areas.
Mountains__tooltip: Mountains support unusually rich ecological diversity because their steep often isolated terrain. Mountains support many different habitats divided by elevation ranges and the direction a slope faces.
Hills__tooltip: Hills are often natural bridges between lowlands and uplands. Their varied slopes, soils, and moisture conditions create a mix of often overlapping habitats with relatively high levels of biodiversity.
Tablelands__tooltip: Tablelands include broad plateaus, canyonlands, mesas, buttes, and sky islands. Strong contrasts between high upland surfaces and lower surrounding terrain divide habitats by limiting movement between them.
Plains__tooltip: Plains are wide, relatively flat landscapes found at many elevations. They often have less ecological variety per unit of area than other landforms, but they can be extremely productive.
landCoverMiniMap__tooltip: In the context of ecosystem settings, land cover represents the most general type of ecological response to the opportunities landform and climate provide.
Water__tooltip: Visible water including lakes, ponds, rivers, reservoirs, wetlands, and oceans. These are vital to life because they provide drinking water, habitat, food, and movement pathways.
Forest__tooltip: Tree-dominated landscapes with continuous or nearly continuous deciduous or evergreen tree canopy.
Shrubland__tooltip: Landscapes with discontinuous or semi-continuous patches of woody shrubs, typically under five meters in height occur.
Grassland__tooltip: Grasslands are continuous areas of short, tall, wet, mixed, non-woody grasses. Land cover data does not distinguish similar, but ecologically distinct areas of rhizomes or savannahs.
Sparsely or Non-Vegetated__tooltip: Includes areas of sparse moss, lichens, or other small plant species. Also included are bare areas that lack soil. These landscapes are often too dry, or too cold to support other vegetation.
Cropland__tooltip: Land used primarily to grow crops for food, fiber, or other agricultural products. Natural vegetation has largely been replaced by cultivated plants.
Settlement__tooltip: Areas where buildings, roads, and other human-made structures dominate the landscape. This includes cities, towns, suburbs, and other infrastructure.
Inow or Ice__tooltip: Land that is covered year-round or most of the year by permanent snow, glaciers, or ice sheets.
climateRegionMinimap__tooltip: In the context of ecosystem settings, climate regions are areas of similar average temperatures and precipitation levels over the course of a typical year.
Tropical Moist__tooltip: Areas without frost and the daily mean annual temperature ranges from 24°C (75°F) to 34°C (93°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is 0.65 or higher, which means irrigation is not required to grow crops.
Tropical Dry__tooltip: Areas without frost and the daily mean annual temperature ranges from 24°C (75°F) to 34°C (93°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is between 0.05 and 0.65, which includes semi-arid and arid areas.
Tropical Desert__tooltip: Areas without frost and the daily mean annual temperature ranges from 24°C (75°F) to 34°C (93°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is below 0.05, or hyperarid.
Subtropical Moist__tooltip: Areas where at least 8 months have an average daily temperature of at least 10°C (50°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is 0.65 or higher, which means irrigation is not required to grow crops.
Subtropical Dry__tooltip: Areas where at least 8 months have an average daily temperature of at least 10°C (50°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is between 0.05 and 0.65, which includes semi-arid and arid areas.
Subtropical Desert__tooltip: Areas where at least 8 months have an average daily temperature of at least 10°C (50°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is below 0.05, or hyperarid.
Warm Temperate Moist__tooltip: Areas where at least 6 months have an average daily temperature of at least 10°C (50°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is 0.65 or higher, which means irrigation is not required to grow crops.
Warm Temperate Dry__tooltip: Areas where at least 6 months have an average daily temperature of at least 10°C (50°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is between 0.05 and 0.65, which includes semi-arid and arid areas.
Warm Temperate Desert__tooltip: Areas where at least 6 months have an average daily temperature of at least 10°C (50°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is below 0.05, or hyperarid.
Cool Temperate Moist__tooltip: Areas where at least 4 months have an average daily temperature of at least 10°C (50°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is 0.65 or higher, which means irrigation is not required to grow crops.
Cool Temperate Dry__tooltip: Areas where at least 4 months have an average daily temperature of at least 10°C (50°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is between 0.05 and 0.65, which includes semi-arid and arid areas.
Cool temperate Desert__tooltip: Areas where at least 4 months have an average daily temperature of at least 10°C (50°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is below 0.05, or hyperarid.
Boreal Moist_tooltip: Areas where at least 3 months have an average daily temperature of at least 10°C (50°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is 0.65 or higher, which means irrigation is not required to grow crops.
Boreal Dry__tooltip: Areas where at least 3 months have an average daily temperature of at least 10°C (50°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is between 0.05 and 0.65, which includes semi-arid and arid areas.
Boreal Desert__tooltip: Areas where at least 3 months have an average daily temperature of at least 10°C (50°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is below 0.05, or hyperarid.
Polar Moist__tooltip: Areas where the average daily temperature is less than 10°C (50°F) year-round, and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is 0.65 or higher, which means irrigation is not required to grow crops.
Polar Dry__tooltip: Areas where the average daily temperature is less than 10°C (50°F) year-round, and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is between 0.05 and 0.65, which includes semi-arid and arid areas.
Hyperthermal Dry__tooltip: Areas without frost and the daily mean annual temperature is higher than 34°C (93°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is between 0.05 and 0.65, which includes semi-arid and arid areas.
Hyperthermal Desert__tooltip: Areas without frost and the daily mean annual temperature is higher than 34°C (93°F), and the relative moisture expressed as aridity index is below 0.05, or hyperarid.
